blocks.text: Battle erupts before the Sikhs can complete their preparations, so suddenly did the fight start with swords and arrows that organized maneuver gives way to immediate resistance. Even under surprise, the Singhs stood their ground fighting hard, treating the clash as a defense of faith, families, and honor rather than as a simple skirmish.

Losses mount quickly in the foremost ranks, and the fighting swirls across the field with muskets, blades, and mounted charges breaking any stable line. The page does not soften the chaos; it presents the combat as a brutal test of endurance in which survival depends on constant regrouping.

Recognizing that the whole community cannot remain fixed in one killing ground, the Sikh leaders decide that Towards the Malwa region should they move their contingents under experienced guidance. Standards are improvised, escorts are assigned, and the struggle becomes both a battle and a desperate attempt to move the vulnerable caravan to safety.
